title: Detect a loop in LL
stepTitle: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
category: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
problemStatement: Detect whether a linked list contains a cycle.
intuition: In a cycle the fast pointer gains one position per step on the slow pointer, so it must eventually land on it. Without a cycle, fast simply falls off the end.

approaches.title: Brute: hash set of visited nodes
Optimal: Floyd's tortoise and hare
approaches.idea: Slow by one, fast by two; meeting means a cycle.
approaches.dryRun:
1->2->3->4->2
slow 1,2,3 / fast 1,3,2 ... they meet inside the loop -> True
approaches.whyWorks: The gap closes by exactly one each step, so it reaches zero within the cycle length.

commonMistakes: Comparing node values instead of identities
patternRecognition: Floyd's algorithm also finds duplicates in arrays treated as functional graphs
followUps: Find the duplicate number in an array with the same technique
interviewInsight: Be ready to prove why they must meet — "the gap shrinks by one per step" is the one-line argument.

related.title: Find the starting point in LL
